desc: A complete standalone cylindrical bark-and-hide arrow container with a closed wooden base, plain capped mouth, and one broad shoulder strap; empty, with no arrows, bow, bow limb, bowstring, or archery set.
historical_anchor: Archaic organic quiver construction; silhouette constrained by the Subeixi/Scythian leather quiver, 8th-3rd century BC.

desc: A complete tapered rawhide quiver with a stiffened rim, fitted hide cap, reinforced bottom, and broad carrying strap; empty standalone container only, no arrows or bow-shaped object.
historical_anchor: Leather quiver and carrying equipment preserved with the Subeixi/Scythian panoply, 8th-3rd century BC.

desc: A long sewn-leather quiver with a narrow hammered-copper mouth band, rigid base cup, restrained edge binding, and one load-bearing strap; capped and empty, no bow or arrows.
historical_anchor: Achaemenid gorytos copper fitting from Deve Huyuk, 5th-4th century BC, adapted to a separate quiver mouth and base.

desc: A complete rigid quiver of tightly bundled reed under dark mineral lacquer, with a broad leather back strip, bronze rim, flush lid, and compact side strap; empty, no arrows, no bow.
historical_anchor: Scythian and Achaemenid structured quiver evidence; organic body is a conservative reconstruction around surviving fittings and depictions.

desc: A severe dark-hide quiver stiffened by three plain raw skymetal ribs, with a deep capped mouth, solid base shoe, and broad shoulder harness; active-service finish, empty, no arrows or bow.
historical_anchor: Otherworldly ladder rung retaining the proportions and stitched fitting logic of the Achaemenid gorytos find.

desc: A complete empty combined bowcase-quiver container in thick sewn hide, with the characteristic asymmetric stepped outline, closed mouth covers, lower beak, and broad suspension strap; absolutely no bow, arrows, string, or loose missiles.
historical_anchor: Early steppe combined bowcase-quiver form shown in art and surviving fittings; Achaemenid example from Deve Huyuk.

desc: A standalone empty leather gorytos with an asymmetric double-lobed body, stitched copper beak-shaped lower fitting, reinforced mouth, and wide belt-and-shoulder harness; no bow, arrows, or bow-shaped accessory.
historical_anchor: Achaemenid copper beak fitting pierced for stitching to a gorytos, 5th-4th century BC.

desc: A complete structured hide gorytos with a broad bowcase lobe, narrow quiver lobe, plain bronze edge plates, closed top flaps, and strong diagonal suspension; empty container only, no contents.
historical_anchor: Scythian/Achaemenid gorytos construction evidenced by the Deve Huyuk fitting and contemporary depictions.

desc: A dark lacquered-wood and hide gorytos with a clean crescent outer profile, small protected obsidian edge insets confined to the base, bronze mouth rims, and broad harness; capped and empty, no bow or arrows.
historical_anchor: Ritual/exotic extrapolation from Achaemenid stitched gorytos geometry, with brittle stone restricted to protected inset fields.

desc: A large empty gorytos of black hide over a thin wood core, with one raw skymetal beak shoe, two plain structural ribs, flush mouth covers, and a heavy load-bearing strap; no bow, arrows, string, or loose gear.
historical_anchor: Otherworldly rung preserving the stitched metal-beak interface of the excavated Achaemenid fitting.

desc: A thick natural cattle horn with a cut blowing tip, one tight secondary rawhide carry loop, and plain scraped surface; complete rugged signal instrument with no metal ornament, runes, or trophy mount.
historical_anchor: Animal-horn signal instruments are a deep-prehistory survival; taxonomy family WC-01.

desc: A compact deep wood-shell drum with one taut hide head, broad carrying strap, and one substantial wood beater secured against the side; plain field instrument, not a modern marching drum.
historical_anchor: Portable frame and signal drums are ancient; construction is a conservative hide-over-wood form.

desc: A heavy cast-bronze handled frame rattle with three transverse sounding rods and a few thick loose plates; plain arch geometry, no deity face, solar disk, readable symbol, or delicate charm cluster.
historical_anchor: Late Period Egyptian/Cypriot bronze sistrum construction, 750-500 BC.

desc: A full-length straight narrow bronze signal tube with a clear mouthpiece and restrained flared bell, shown tip to bell on a steep diagonal; joined-sheet construction, no valves, coils, or medieval horn fittings.
historical_anchor: Etruscan straight bronze trumpet, 4th-3rd century BC.

desc: A powerful near-circular raw dark skymetal signal horn with a rigid cross-brace, clear mouthpiece, broad bell, and complete compact tubing; plain severe surfaces, no glow, spikes, heraldry, or medieval brasswork.
historical_anchor: Roman cornu/buccina braced circular signal-horn geometry, translated to the endgame material rung.

desc: A full-length narrow hardwood rally pole carrying one perforated naturally forked red-deer antler crown seated over the pole tip and bound through the perforation; no cloth, weapon point, totem carving, or loose trophies.
historical_anchor: Explicit lore-archaic faction invention; the load path derives from Neolithic/Bronze Age perforated antler mace-head construction rather than a claimed surviving standard.

desc: A full-length thick wood standard with a transverse wood crossbar seated in a forked pole top and tightly lashed, supporting one bounded rectangular rawhide panel pierced and cord-bound along its upper edge; no horn crosspiece, polearm point, or flowing pennon.
historical_anchor: Conservative perishable-material reconstruction based on the ancient vexillum crossbar-and-bounded-panel form documented in Roman stone depiction.

desc: A full-length narrow ash standard pole carrying one substantial socketed cast-bronze open geometric finial above a wrapped hand zone; one motif only, no figures, faces, sun disks, weapon point, or cloth.
historical_anchor: Iron Age Luristan socketed bronze standard-finial, 9th-8th century BC.

desc: A full-length bronze-capped pole and sturdy crossbar supporting one bounded rectangular madder cloth panel with a plain woven border; complete weapon-length standard, no text, emblem, eagle, tassel cloud, spear point, or flowing medieval pennon.
historical_anchor: Roman vexillum crossbar construction documented by an AD 138-161 stone depiction from Corbridge.

desc: A full-length dark-wood standard with a raw skymetal fork crown holding one taut rectangular crimson hide panel inside the fork; severe plain construction, no glow, heraldry, solar mark, spear tip, or medieval pennon silhouette.
historical_anchor: Endgame material translation of the bounded Roman standard-panel structure with a rigid non-weapon fork crown.

desc: A complete light bentwood backboard with two shoulder straps, side tension cords, and a secured rolled hide cover; clearly wearable load-bearing gear, no torso, purse, handles, modern backpack body, or metal hardware.
historical_anchor: Chalcolithic carrying-frame interpretation associated with Ötzi's reconstructed backpack equipment.

desc: A narrow wood backboard with broad shoulder harness, flank strap, and three capped reed dart tubes secured beneath small copper collars; worn rig, not a handheld case, quiver, briefcase, or modern bag.
historical_anchor: Ancient dart-carry systems and early copper fittings; body-mounting follows conservative back-frame construction.

desc: A complete bronze-braced wood backboard with shoulder harness and side straps, carrying three squat lidded ceramic medicine cups and a compact folded instrument roll; all contents secured, no handles or luggage silhouette.
historical_anchor: Roman bronze medical instruments paired with an ancient wearable frame rather than a modern doctor's bag.

desc: A clean lacquered-wood flank frame with broad body strap, narrow lidded point case, wax cup, cord spool, and protected feather backing; low-snag worn carrier, no arrows, bow, loose feathers, purse flap, or suitcase handle.
historical_anchor: Ancient archery maintenance kit extrapolated from Scythian quiver equipment and archaeological gorytos fittings.

desc: A rigid dark-wood backboard edged by two plain raw skymetal braces, with complete shoulder harness, side straps, and compact secured trigger plates, short pegs, tinder cup, and coiled snare line; no bag or briefcase form.
historical_anchor: Endgame Quick Rig retaining prehistoric back-frame mechanics and ancient field-component materials.

desc: A compact hide-wrapped preparation containing short hardwood pegs, a flat trigger tongue, and one neatly coiled plant-fiber snare line on a rigid bark backing; no sprung steel jaws, wire, modern cable, or loose clutter.
historical_anchor: Perishable lore-archaic snare technology; component geometry corroborated by simple cane-and-fiber ethnographic snares, not back-dated as an artifact.

desc: A flat wood carrier board holding two notched trigger sticks, one short prop, braided cord, and a palm-sized stone weight in fitted recesses; coherent ancient field kit, no finished trap scene or modern mechanism.
historical_anchor: Simple deadfall trigger is a conservative perishable-technology reconstruction; stone and cord roles remain mechanically explicit.

desc: A tight folded flax net on a stiff leather backing with a row of pierced clay sinkers, two short setting pegs, and one coiled retrieval cord; portable preparation object, no animal, gore, steel chain, or modern fishing reel.
historical_anchor: New Kingdom handmade perforated clay net sinker from Amara West, Nubia.

desc: A divided lacquered-wood flank case holding three pierced fired-clay weights, two notched hardwood trigger tongues, two short setting pegs, and a compact plant-fiber cord coil; no lead bullets, metal trigger parts, spring jaws, wire, or modern latch.
historical_anchor: New Kingdom perforated clay net sinker from Amara West anchors the weights; the notched wood trigger is a conservative perishable-component reconstruction.

desc: A compact dark-hide case on a thin raw-skymetal backing plate, opened to show one heavy cord coil, three plain trigger plates, short pegs, and a flint striker in fitted compartments; no modern tools, hinges, springs, wire, or briefcase handle.
historical_anchor: Endgame material translation of ancient fire, cord, peg, and weighted-trigger preparation families.

desc: A folded rawhide fire packet opened just enough to show a flint flake, iron-pyrite nodule, dry tinder fungus, and one fiber nest; one compact prepared object, no matches, lighter, glass vial, or modern pouch styling.
historical_anchor: Ötzi's Chalcolithic fire-making equipment and carried tinder provide the construction anchor.

desc: A small deep stone mortar with a hand-length pestle, two cleaned dried roots, and a folded linen measure nested as one compact set; practical preparation gear, no bottle shop clutter or modern labels.
historical_anchor: Ancient mortar-and-pestle medicine/cosmetic practice; simple stone vessel technology spans prehistory onward.

desc: A compact divided shallow wood case with two mineral pigment cakes, a small rectangular stone mixing palette, short bronze spatula, and tightly fitted pyxis; no readable writing, paint tubes, brushes, or modern artist box.
historical_anchor: Roman stone ointment palette and Early Cycladic pigment-bearing pyxis.

desc: A compact complete two-piece bronze cosmetic grinder with one grooved mortar and matching curved pestle nested together on a fitted backing; plain tool geometry, no celestial motif, text, modern cosmetics, or glass laboratory gear.
historical_anchor: Late Iron Age/Roman two-piece cosmetic grinder, a distinctive archaeological preparation-tool family.

desc: A compact dark hide instrument roll opened to show a few raw skymetal probes, forceps, spatula, bone needle, and clean linen in fitted loops; ancient forms only, no scissors, syringe, steel shine, modern medical bag, or loose container clutter.
historical_anchor: Roman bronze forceps and the British Museum corpus of Greek and Roman medical instruments.

desc: A fist-sized river stone held in a rigid antler-and-cord cage, hovering just above one small bone whorl; two-part magical focus with restrained pale light, no hand, pedestal, currency-token swarm, or abstract crystal.
historical_anchor: Attendant AT-04 derived from ancient sling stones, weights, cages, and spindle whorls.

desc: A short horizontal copper axle with one heavy spindle whorl and one offset ring counter-rotating around it in impossible suspension; complete robust mechanism, no gears, clockwork, modern bearings, or loose coin-like pieces.
historical_anchor: Early Helladic terracotta spindle whorl, ca. 3000-2000 BC; Verdigris-magical reinterpretation AT-06.

desc: One substantial bronze bell hovering beneath a compact forked yoke, with visible clapper and two taut self-supporting suspension arms; plain authority object, no charm cluster, chains, deity face, text, or solar symbol.
historical_anchor: Greek leaded-bronze bell with surviving internal clapper, 3rd-4th century BC; Attendant family AT-14.

desc: A squat lidded greenstone pyxis floating in two clean pieces, lid and body counter-rotating around one narrow inner light seam; vessel remains materially solid, no loose gems, orbiting coins, runes, or modern precision machining.
historical_anchor: Early Cycladic lidded pyxis proportions, 2800-2700 BC, translated into Attendant family AT-12.

desc: A raw dark skymetal upright rectangular open frame floating without chains, with three oil-light cups on staggered alternating side arms and one heavy lower counterweight; asymmetric pierced-and-riveted construction, no wheel, radial spokes, halo, chandelier crystals, Gothic tracery, or modern machinery.
historical_anchor: Early Byzantine polycandelon multiple-lamp construction, AD 500-600, deliberately reorganized into a non-radial Attendant frame.

desc: A palm-sized folded hide parcel opened to reveal one dry nonhuman bone fragment wrapped in clean ochre cloth and plain cord; preserved relic, no gore, human anatomy, jewelry mounting, metal cap, or display pedestal.
historical_anchor: Lore-archaic wrapped relic family RL-13; organic preservation and textile binding are conservative ancient practices.

desc: A deep cylindrical carved-wood pyxis with thick walls, fitted lid, and one small cloth-wrapped interior fragment visible beside it; plain concentric rim bands only, no spiral, readable text, cross, or miniature shrine.
historical_anchor: Early Cycladic cylindrical pyxis, 2800-2700 BC, supplies the container proportions.

desc: A tall cylindrical cast copper-alloy reliquary with a slightly convex base and long close-fitting domed lid, wrapped in taut plain silk gathered against the lid sides and fixed by several small wax seals along the upper edge; no handles, hinges, feet, corner straps, lock plate, figures, script, gemstones, or medieval chest form.
historical_anchor: Kushan copper-alloy reliquary from the Manikyala Great Stupa foundation deposit, probably 2nd century AD; the British Museum record documents its cylindrical body, slightly convex base, long domed lid, and former taut silk wrapping sealed with wax.

desc: A flattened fired-clay flask with pierced shoulders, narrow mouth, and one small protected flat jade inset on the reinforced shoulder bridge; complete and stoppered, with no carved greenstone body, copied sacred image, cross, face, script, halo, or sun disk.
historical_anchor: Early Byzantine pierced-shoulder clay pilgrim ampulla, 5th-6th century AD; the T4 exotic material is limited to one protected non-structural inset.

desc: A compact raw skymetal lidded censer with a deep bowl, perforated lid in plain chevron openings, short three-arm suspension crown, and one folded relic cloth within; no Gothic cage, long chains, cross, incense smoke, or ornate filigree.
historical_anchor: Late Roman/Early Byzantine chained censer construction anchors the bowl, lid, and three-arm suspension.

desc: One dry split section of an aurochs femur, washed and scraped with one broad usable wall and a rough cloth wrap only around the broken end; raw bone-working stock, no carving, polish, mounting, jewelry, gore, joint, hoof, or whole limb.
historical_anchor: Mesolithic worked aurochs femur from Star Carr, ca. 8000 BC, also preserving evidence of skin-preparation use.

desc: Three naturally mismatched wild-boar tusk sections bundled in one rough hide packet with the tips visible; dry saleable tooth stock, no necklace cord, polish, drilling, precious fittings, blood, jaw, or creature face.
historical_anchor: Neolithic/Bronze Age boar-tusk working and perforation from the Goodmanham barrow find.

desc: One irregular dry patch of overlapping Nile-crocodile dorsal scutes still attached to scraped hide, washed and folded once under a plain fiber band; raw armor stock, no backing, rivets, gilding, display mount, head, limb, flesh, or gore.
historical_anchor: Roman-period sewn crocodile-skin armor from Manfalut, 3rd-4th century AD, demonstrates the specific hide material in equipment use.

desc: One long dry red-deer antler beam segment trimmed free of the cranium, with two sawn tine bases, one naturally broken working end, and a plain fiber band around the rough cut; raw antler-working stock, no skull, face, whole head, polished carving, metal cap, display mount, gore, or trophy presentation.
historical_anchor: Late Bronze Age red-deer hunted-antler working waste from Runnymede Bridge, 900-700 BC, with sawn tines and working traces.

desc: One heavy irregular raw iron meteorite nodule with a dark fusion crust and one naturally broken metallic face, resting in a coarse transport cloth; unworked skymetal stock, no polish, etched crystal pattern, carving, glow, socket, pedestal, or jewelry.
historical_anchor: Raw iron-meteorite specimen morphology from the Natural History Museum meteorite collection; T5 stock replaces the former T4 obsidian mismatch.
